sentences.text: Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This is petitioners' appeal filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) seeking enhancement of compensation granted for the death of one Jambanna in a motor vehicle accident dated 03.11.2016.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. Petitioners are the wife, children and parents of deceased Jambanna.

It is the case of the petitioners that on 03.11.2016 at about 3-00 p.m., the deceased Jambanna was proceeding from KPC main gate, towards first cross by riding XL Super Moped bearing registration No.KA-33/R-8738 ('Moped' for short).

The driver of lorry bearing registration No.HA-61/A-6929 ('offending vehicle' for short) came in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner from Hyderabad side and while overtaking another vehicle, dashed against the Moped of the deceased.
As a result of the accident, Jambanna sustained grievous injuries and became unconscious.

He was treated at RIMS hospital, Raichur, Suraksha hospital, Raichur, Apollo hospital, Hyderabad, V.S. Achar Multi Smt. Neelamma And Ors vs Jitender And Anr on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160238106/

sentences.text: Speciality hospital and NIMHANS hospital, Bengaluru.
However, he succumbed to the injuries on 23.11.2016.
As the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

5. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 have filed separate written statement disputing the age, occupation,
income of the deceased and also that petitioners were dependent on him.
They have disputed that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

Respondent No.2 has further contended that at the time of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence and as such, it is not liable to indemnify respondent No.1 and prays to dismiss the petition.
6.
Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.

7. On behalf of the petitioners, petitioner No.1 is examined as P.W.1, two witnesses as P.W.2 and 3 and Exs.P1 to 50 are marked.
8.
On behalf of respondent No.2, R.W.1 is examined and Exs.R1 to 7 are marked.

9. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and quantified the compensation at Rs.17,73,797/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.

10. The details of the compensation granted are as under:
 Sl. Head Amount  No. awarded  1. For loss of dependency Rs,7,92,000/-
 2. For loss of consortium Rs.25,000/-

3. For loss of love and Rs.25,000/-

For loss of estate Rs.25,000/-
 5.

For medical expenses Rs.8,43,797/-
 from the date of accident  till death

6. For transportation of Rs.63,000/-
 death body & funeral  expenses
11. Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
12. During the course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the income taken at Rs.8,000/- p.m. is on the lower side.
It has not added any amount towards future prospects.
The compensation granted under the head consortium is on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

14. Heard arguments and perused the records.
15.

Having regard to the fact that the respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and due to the injuries suffered in the said accident, Jambanna died has attained finality.
16. The petitioners claim that at the time of accident, the deceased was aged 45 years.
In fact in PM report also, his age is also noted as 45 years.

However, the Tribunal is not justified in considering the age of the deceased as 51 years on the ground that his eldest son is aged 25 years, whereas the age difference between him and his mother i.e., petitioner No.1 is only 15 years.
It is not uncommon for the villagers especially girls to be married at 14-15 years, though it is prohibited under law.
Therefore, the age of the deceased is taken as 45 years.
Consequently, the appropriate multiplier would be 14.
In the absence of proof of exact income, the Tribunal is justified in considering the income of notional basis.
Since the accident is of the year 2016, the income ought to have been taken at Rs.8,750/- p.m. instead of Rs.8,000/- p.m.
However, the Tribunal has not added any compensation towards loss of future prospects.

Since the deceased was aged 45 years, as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1, (Magma's case), 25% is required to be added towards loss of future prospects.

sentences.text: Therefore, the income is required to be taken at Rs.10,937/-.
Since there are seven dependents, 1/5th is required to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
With these components, the compensation under the head loss of dependency is Rs.10,937 x 12 x 14 x 4/5= 14,69,932/- against Rs.7,92,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

17. As wife, children and parents, petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/-
each i.e., Rs.2,80,000/- under the head loss of consortium as against Rs.25,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
The compensation granted in a sum of Rs.25,000/- under the head loss of love and affection is disallowed.

18. When substantial compensation is granted under the head loss of dependency, as per National Insurance Company Limited V. Pranay Sethi and others2 (Pranay Sethi's case) and Magma cases,
Rs.15,000/- each is required to be granted under the head (2017) 16 SCC 680 loss to estate and funeral expenses (which includes transportation charge).

20. Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.26,23,729/- as against Rs.17,73,797/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum as detailed below:

(ii) Appellants/petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.26,23,729/-
